body:
Found reviewing #250.

`report_hydrate_grounding.py` scans `preferred_term` only. The hydrate notation this corpus uses most exotically lives in **synonyms**, where the report cannot see it:

| separator | occurrences in synonyms | in preferred_term |
|---|---|---|
| `・` U+30FB | 74 | 0 |
| `⋅` U+22C5 | 29 | 0 |
| `∙` U+2219 | 18 | 0 |
| `×` U+00D7 | 13 | 0 |

**18 mapped records carry a hydrate-notated synonym while their `preferred_term` is the anhydrous form**, for example:

```
CHEBI:3312   "CaCl2"       synonym: CaCl2 × 2 H2O
CHEBI:35696  "CoCl2"       synonym: CoCl2 × 6H2O
CHEBI:17561  "L-Cysteine"  synonym: Cysteine-HCl∙H2O
```

That is the #218 identity collapse **after** a merge: the hydrate was folded into the anhydrous record as a synonym rather than given its own identifier. MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md Section 3 says a hydration state is a distinct substance, so a hydrate label should not be a synonym of the anhydrous term — it should be its own record with a hydrate-specific term or its own `cas:` id.

## Why the report misses it

Both loops in `report_hydrate_grounding.py` key on `preferred_term`. Since #229 publishes synonyms, these labels *do* resolve from `docs/data/all_ingredients.csv` — to the anhydrous parent, which is exactly the wrong answer and is invisible to every current check:

- `qc-duplicate-ids` sees one identifier, one record — no duplicate.
- `qc-flat-coverage` sees the label published — coverage satisfied.
- `report-hydrate-grounding` never looks at synonyms.

## Suggested fix

Add a third bucket to the report: mapped records whose `preferred_term` is not a hydrate but which carry a hydrate-notated synonym. Then decide per record whether to split the synonym out into its own record (Section 3) or, where the synonym is merely a spelling of the same hydration state the record already represents, leave it.

Worth checking against the 15 merges in #226 and the 9 in #214 — some of these may be merges that should not have happened, in which case they need the same treatment `merge-ingredients`' Scenario 3 now describes.

Related: #250, #247, #218, #225, #229.

comments.body:
Reporting shipped in #253 (see that PR for what the review corrected). `just report-hydrate-grounding` now lists the 16 records whose term is anhydrous but which carry a hydrate synonym, with the full synonym lists in `reports/hydrate_synonyms.tsv`, and says which are already tracked in the duplicate-identifier baseline — **10 known, 5 new to any check**.

Keeping this open for the **triage**: per Section 3 most of the 16 should be split out with their own identifier, but several came from merges in #214/#226 that may need reversing, and some synonyms are just another spelling of the hydration state the record already represents.

The related population — records whose own label is a hydrate but which carry a synonym naming a *different* hydration state — is **#254**. I attempted it here and shipped 96 findings that were almost all false, so it needs a tested multiplicity parser first.

title: Hydrate notation hidden in synonyms is invisible to every hydrate check
